Kipferl 0.7.2 refreshes the 1,000-package audit and makes its release packaging
runtime-specific. Every release CLI now carries results generated against its
own embedded runtime and platform, alongside the separately reviewed package
compatibility catalog.

## Refreshed findings

The local candidate rerun examined all 1,000 ranked projects using the same 999
available release/artifact metadata pins as the previous screen. Results were
unchanged: 44 distributions completed compilation, including 24 with Python
source and 20 with no Python source. There were 770 syntax blockers, 178
native-wheel blockers, five Python-version conflicts, one source-only release,
and two explicit audit limits. No first syntax blocker changed.

Compilation completion is not proof that a package works. This broad audit does
not execute imports, dependency closures, package behavior, or setup/build code.
The limits remain awscli's expanded wheel and ddtrace's oversized metadata;
ddtrace has no reusable metadata pin and is fetched again under the same bound.

## Release changes

- Rerun the full audit separately against all four native release runtimes.
- Embed the matching full report and exact syntax-blocker catalog in each CLI.
  `kipferl deps audit --json` exports the report without a project or network.
- Publish per-platform JSON, CSV, and syntax catalogs with SHA-256 sidecars.
  The shared ranking snapshot and metadata pins are also attached with checksums.
  Reject incomplete coverage, runtime/platform mismatches, changed metadata
  pins, inconsistent exports, and unresolved network errors before packaging.
- Keep reviewed behavior evidence separate. Only those explicitly reviewed
  tests can produce a tested package record.
- Update the searchable website, documentation, and before/after comparison.

The pinned ranking describes August 2026 PyPI download counts. Package releases
are selected at the recorded metadata-fetch time; older releases and alternative
wheels are outside this screen. Consult the attached platform report for the
exact runtime hash, metadata manifest identity, coverage, and findings.

## Upgrade

Run `brew update && brew upgrade kipferl`, or download your platform's binary
and verify its adjacent checksum. `kipferl --version` reports `Kipferl v0.7.2`.
The recorded website demonstration remains correctly labeled 0.7.1; its project,
package, and standalone workflow is unchanged.

Runtime-bound dependency locks may need refreshing: rerun `kipferl add` for
declared requirements, review and commit the lock, then run application tests.
Never edit hashes to bypass a mismatch.

Audit and evidence: https://kipferl.dev/docs/guides/package-audit
